changes.summary: For one week - later extended by three -, the Musée d’Orsay is thinking big to showcase the visual world of the video game "Clair Obscur: Expedition 33". Thanks to an innovative display, the central aisle of the main gallery is adorned with in-game screenshots and concept art (preliminary sketches), some of which have never been seen before. All those images share deep aesthetic connections with the museum’s collections. Painting is a constant presence throughout the story of Clair Obscur: Expedition 33. It establishes the antagonist’s role from the very beginning of the plot and continues to add depth to the narrative right up to its conclusion. This exhibition aims to shed light on a few—sometimes hidden—references and trans-historical echoes: from the glistening cobblestones of Gustave Caillebotte’s Rue de Paris, temps de pluie, echoed by the reflections of textures on the streets of Lumière’s imagined city, all the way to Victor Navlet’s A bird's-eye view of Paris, taken from the Observatory in a hot-air balloon, rendered from Esquie’s aerial perspective. The architecture of the Orsay and Monoco train stations echoes one another, while iconic public monuments and street furniture mirror each other between Paris and Lumière. The creative team behind Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 drew inspiration from the iconography found in the Musée d’Orsay’s collections, reimagining its iconic symbols: a fractured Eiffel Tower and Arc de Triomphe, the Wallace Fountains transformed into statues, and Carpeaux’s The Four Parts of the World supporting the celestial sphere, shattered into pieces... For a new audience, the name “Renoir” now also evokes the patriarch of the Dessendre family.
